chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The purchase of the 'Gharar of theft' and the 'Gharar of treachery' is not valid when they are known."
ai.seo_question: What is Gharar al-Sariqah and Gharar al-Khiyanah in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of *Gharar* (uncertainty) in trade is specifically triggered when the risk of theft or treachery is known, distinguishing it from general commercial risk. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on transparency and fairness, ensuring that buyers are not deceived by concealed liabilities in commercial contracts.
